q: How much coke does an efficient 600 kg pit furnace save in brass melting?
title: Efficient 600 kg pit furnace: coke saved
short: BEE's Jagadhri design cuts a 600 kg brass pit furnace from 96 to 81.6 t of coke a year, saving 14.4 t, by rounding the pit and preheating the charge with flue gas. At the IPCC coke factor that is 43.5 t CO2, more than the report's 39 t. Cost Rs 0.95 lakh.
audience: Brass melting units in Jagadhri and other clusters using coke-fired pit furnaces

p: A rectangular pit lined with refractory and faced with red brick, coke fed from below and the sides, a 1 HP blower. It melts 600 kg a batch on 80 kg of coke, four batches a day for 300 days: 96 t of coke. Melt temperature was 1,021 °C, flue gas 500 to 550 °C, efficiency 11.4%, and about 20 kg of coke was left unburnt each batch.

sections.h: Two changes, half the saving each
ul: Rounded corners: the pit shrinks from 0.312 to 0.297 m3, so 7.4% less coke fills the space around the crucible: 7.1 t a year.
Waste heat recovery: flue gas cooled from 500 to 200 °C in an exchanger at 65% effectiveness preheats the charge: 7.81%, or 7.3 t a year.
Together 14.4 t, 15%. The report also says efficiency rises from 11.4% to 13%, which alone would be about 12%; treat 15% as an estimate to measure.

p: Rs 0.75 lakh for the furnace with heat recovery plus Rs 0.20 lakh for civil work. At the report's Rs 22,000 a tonne, 14.4 t is Rs 3.17 lakh a year: payback in under four months. If the real saving is half the estimate, payback is still about seven months.

If unburnt coke is raked out and charged again, 80 kg a batch counts it twice. Work out CO2 from coke bought plus opening stock minus closing stock, which is also what a lender or buyer can check against invoices.

example.title: CO2 per year and per tonne of brass
lines: Saved: 14.4 t x 3.02 = 43.5 t CO2 a year
Per tonne melted: 133 kg coke (403 kg CO2) falls to 113 kg (342 kg CO2)
example.note: Coke at the IPCC 2006 default, 107,000 kg CO2 per TJ at 28.2 GJ per tonne, an estimate. Furnace figures from BEE's 2010 report.

senseible: Senseible reads coke invoices and electricity bills into dated monthly records linked to each bill. It has no built-in coke factor, so apply the IPCC figure above to the tonnes. The green loan check shows what a lender asks for on a furnace upgrade.
